text: Our meetup group Matters of Taste visited Cholita Taqueria on 5/19/19 for their unlimited Sunday brunch. Members enjoyed it so much that a return was planned for today Memorial Day since they closed on Sunday probably due to the race traffic. Unfortunately it was a disaster! We arrived promptly at 11 a.m. when the doors opened. Since there were 16 in our party in an effort to be less bother to the kitchen we decided to order as a group so everyone could taste multiple items on the menu. Immediately upon arrival our organizer put in our appetizer order for the table; 3 orders of Queso Fundido, some Mexican Street Corn and 3 Breakfast Tlayuda. I would assume that this was one of the first orders sent into the kitchen if not the first. The Breakfast Tlayuda's were large and 3 of them allowed everyone in our group to sample it. Not bad...nice and crunchy with lots of toppings. The Queso Fundido while a bit crispy on the outer edge was far from being hot and bubbly...in fact the cheese in the middle wasn't even melted!! We each passed around the ears of corn and cut some off the cob and boy was it delicious!! Prior to her unexpected departure Sigi had also placed an order for 16 Baja Fish Tacos and consulted with the group and asked our waiter to put in an order again for the table of '64 total items'...which our waiter then advised us that he didn't even give to the kitchen staff as 'an order for that many items would overwhelm them and no-one else would get any food'. This was a recurring theme from him and my thought was that if your restaurant seats x number of people and you offer an unlimited brunch you should be able to execute it even if every seat in the house is filled vs beating up on patrons who are there paying your wages. It was as though he expected an apology from us because we were there 'keeping others from getting their food'...not a great feeling. Considering that if each of the 16 of us would have placed an order individually for assorted tacos of our choice the kitchen would have had to prepare 32 tacos...not just 16 of one type so I found this to be very strange. Oh and I didn't mention that the ONLY food we were served in 1 1/2 hours were the shared appetizers and fish tacos mentioned above. At this point several of our party paid their checks and left. Our waiter then asked if we wanted to move down and consolidate, but he never bussed the table so we could do so. Finally, I pushed some glassed, plates, etc to the end of the table and wiped it down myself so we could squeeze together. We were then advised by our waiter he would take orders from each of us individually for one item off of the menu at a time. So we each placed an order for one item. Then we waited and waited and waited some more. No food came out from the kitchen. Then our waiter came back and told us to just go ahead and order 2 or 3 items each. At that point I wasn't sure what was happening to our orders...was the kitchen staff throwing them away...was he just not turning them in...perplexing. Personally, I placed an order for myself 4 times for the Mexican Style Crispy Chicken Milanese Sliders. i also requested the Sweet Corn Tamales and an order of Cinnamon Churros. At around 2 hours into our dining experience food began being delivered to our table. The Sweet Corn Tamales were outstanding but the Milanese Chicken Sliders weren't sliders at all. The sandwich was actually served on bread I normally associate with Cuban sandwiches. Since I had been warned about the spice level I was surprised that there was no heat to this sandwich at all which makes me wonder if it was prepared correctly. The chicken itself was crispy around the edges but soggy in the middle. Not something I would order again. At 2 1/2 hours after the manager became involved we did receive several Chocolate Mexican Waffles and orders of Churros, along with to-go boxes as we all were eager to get on with our other plans for the day. The Churros were pretty typical but the Chocolate Mexican Waffle was the bomb...light airy and with just the right chocolate flavor. Without the intervention of the manager --- thank you, thank you, thank you!! I'm not sure we would have received any food beyond our appetizers and fish tacos. It was also appreciated that he did mark our bills down to help make up for the poor service from the staff. Having hoped for a similar experience as the one our group had on 5/19/19 where they tried virtually every dish on the brunch menu I was a bit disappointed but enough of the food was tasty that I will probably give it another try...however, the beauty of going with a group is the ability to taste more dishes than you would be able to if dining alone or with only a small party. text: Despite the rating, I actually really enjoy the food here. The food is good. The portion sizes are enough for everyone to try a piece of everything without feeling too full. I was considering not writing this review, but I keep thinking about it, and I should probably talk about my experiences. I've been here four times total, with one of them being during soft opening with a group of friends. The food was significantly better during then. The second time was with my sister and the food was still pretty good then, too, but there was a server that kept bothering us about our food. Not really bothering, but she kept asking "how's everything? or "can I help you with everything" which normally would be fine, but if you ask every couple minutes (I'm not exaggerating), then it gets excessive. She literally asked us how everything was while I got started on eating a fish ball and then went to the next table and asked how everything is and then went back to us to ask the same question, and I was still chewing my fish ball. At that point, we started counting how many times she asked, and it was around 10-12 times within a two hour eating period. Please just let me finish my food. The third time I went was fine. I had no complaints except for the wait time which ended up being an hour & a half for four people. I guess that's okay, and it helps that Dave & Buster's is across the street. The fourth time was when I had real issues. It was my first time going during lunch hours, and everything was nice & prompt. I was with my friend who's a vegetarian, and we only opted for hot pot. There's plenty of vegetables and options for vegetarians. We had separate pots, so I could order any meat dish I want without disrupting her diet. We had ordered fried tofu which we both shared and decided that we wanted more. When the second batch arrived, I had noticed that it looked different from the first batch. The server also looked hesitant before placing it down on our table but ended up giving it to us anyway. The first batch looked like those fried soy puffs and the second one looked to me like actual tofu that's been fried which could also resemble fish tofu. I was eating a fish ball before taking a bite of the tofu, so I figured the fishiness was just from my fish ball. I was wrong. My friend who's been vegetarian for six years now took a bite and told me it tasted like fish and spit it back out. I pretty much insisted she was wrong, but I asked the server to come over and double checked with him to see if this was fried tofu and or fish tofu, and his words were "it should be fried tofu, but I can check for you if you want," and I opted not to check because I felt like it was probably just in her head. I was wrong. I took a bite of the tofu after drinking water and became unsure and then finally asked the waiter a second time to go check with the kitchen to see if it's really regular fried tofu. Also, at this point, my friend found a hair in her food (her hair was tied up, so I really don't think it was hers, and it's too short to be either of ours) Waiter came out with good news and bad news with the bad news being that to our dismay, the fried tofu we've been eating was actually fish tofu, and the good news being that we get 10% off our meal. I don't mean to sound entitled but 10% was $3.40. I'd be okay paying full price for my meal since I enjoyed it, but she's vegetarian, and she didn't eat much after finding out the fact that she ate fish. Telling her she gets 10% off her meal doesn't feel redeemable. The manager ended up coming out and apologizing for the hair but said nothing about the fish tofu incident. Overall, I would personally come back because like I said, I enjoy the food, but please watch out if you have any dietary restrictions.

text: Awesome! We had a blast! A few quick tips: Book online. Park in the marina lot and put a quarter in the meter. Head over to H20 and they'll give you a 4 hour parking pass for $4. You'll have time to keep the vehicle parked and grab a bite after the tour. Leave your phone behind; they have secure storage. Tip your guide. We did the tour on a Thursday morning in October. It was my wife and I and another couple. I jokingly told my wife: "I got us a semi private tour!" What we liked about H20 was they had a covered space in the marina. This made filling out paperwork, gearing up, storing your stuff a lot easier. I'm sure you know this by now, but the FLA sun is HOT...even in October. The tour was a blast. We left the marina, went under the causeway bridge and blasted around a few islands. We had time for some free riding mid tour and our guide took pics of us on his phone (he sent them to us right after the tour). On the way back, we went by Clearwater beach. Our guide (William) was awesome! He and I stayed up front and went at a good clip. If the others got a bit behind, he'd do a few circles until they caught up and we were back on the throttles again. They have nice Yamaha machines here. They were all in good shape and well taken care of. Renters were on 1,000cc machines, the guide had the 1,800cc machine. (Wonder if they allow those to be rented? ; ) ) If you are a couple doing this, renting two machines is a good option. It allows everyone to go at their own pace. The couple that was with us stated they wished they went for two machines vs riding two up. All in all, this was a lot of fun! It's one of the things I tell people about back home when they ask: "How was your trip to Clearwater?:

text: Holy moly, Wilson's Secret Sauce lives up to the hype and the sauce itself is bomb af. First off, the husband-wife team who own this spot are SO nice and hospitable. This is the first restaurant they've owned and they've done a terrific job with the setup and atmosphere. It's warm and inviting, and a cute little pig collection arranged to the left of the kitchen, along with some of the other decorations, lends a hint of kitsch. The BBQ dished up here is top tier. We ordered a two meat platter to-go because we couldn't decide between brisket and pulled pork. Let me tell you, the flavors of the roast pork and smokey brisket were insane. Plus, both meats were just so tender and melt-in-your-mouth delicious. The roast pork was incredibly succulent and the brisket cut easy with a butter knife. Generous portions, too! One platter fed two people, and there was even a bit of pulled pork left over. And the Secret Sauce? It was sweet, spicy, tart, zesty, and highly addictive. We unabashedly scraped the two plastic cups clean and I may have licked my fingers... For sides, we picked mac 'n cheese and coleslaw. The stovetop style mac was deceptively cheesy -- I quickly realized that most of the cheese was hiding at the bottom. It was a tasty rendition worth repeating. Getting a bit of meat and mac together on the same fork and then dipping it into the sauce made for an intensely enjoyable bite. The coleslaw unfortunately had way too much mayonnaise for my liking. And I'm a lover of mayo! I also noticed that the cornbread was a little dry. But the cherry cheesecake pudding I picked for dessert? It had me feeling all warm and nostalgic inside. This pudding so reminded me of the Pennsylvania Dutch version of cherries jubilee (aka cherry delight), which I've adored since childhood. The cherries had the ideal tartness, which balanced out the sweetness of the cheesecake pudding. Total bliss. I'm glad I finally visited and I'll certainly be back, probably to dine in next time and chow down on a brisket cheesesteak. The meats I tried here are fantastic, and as the main attraction, they obviously matter most. But I also can't get that Secret Sauce out of my head, and the same goes for the cherry pudding dessert. I was sad to see Rigatoni's Crabcakes shut their doors awhile back, but I'm happy to have Wilson's take their place.

text: We've now been to 4 axe throwing establishments across the country, and Axeventures is the least safe of them all. We made a reservation through Groupon and brought friends who were first-time axe throwers. There were more people than they expected for our reservation time, so we were instructed on how to axe throw as a very large group. There were over a dozen people listening to one instructor. There was minimal instruction, and the instructor did not watch people carefully and actually left! There was pretty much no one-on-one guidance or advice. Most importantly, absolutely NO safety instructions were given. We were also shocked that they recommend throwing axes one-handed, when every other place we've been to has recommended two-handed throwing to start. The entire space is crammed. The lanes are the shortest we've seen, so axes bounce back closely to the thrower and observers. The tables are also too close to the axe throwing! They group two lanes together at a time, so there is no separation between the axe throwing of one group and another. This means that when you go in the cage to retrieve your axe, you have to make sure the group next to you isn't throwing at the same time! The group we shared with was kind, and we timed our throws so we could retrieve axes at the same time, but this set-up is just not safe. The wood is flimsy, and the fencing is not sturdy. The axes are not heavy enough, so they bounce back significantly. At one point during our hour-and-a-half session, it started to smell like cigarette smoke. I think one of the employees took a smoke break in the indoor back room right next to our lane. It smelled awful, and when we brought it up, they sprayed a lot air freshener to try and mask the smell, but it just made everything worse. We had a fun night, because we spent it with great friends, but Axeventures does not handle axe throwing (a fun activity!) in a safe and responsible way. I would not recommend coming here.

Fast forward 1 week, the leather was already horribly distressed and they replaced it for free, great! Awesome customer service, Ian was extraordinary! Fast forward another about month/month and a half later and again the leather is again horribly distressed, not what you expect out of leather as it ages and gets broken in. And the plastic frame that holds your phone in place inside is broken. I get phone cases are used rigorously daily and are subject to high levels of wear and tear but for less than 2 months this is kind of ridiculous to me. When I spoke to a sales associate, I believe her name was Olivia (??), but I don't entirely remember, about my dissatisfaction with the product she gave me the boilerplate response that I just mentioned... "well phone cases do wear out more" so on and so forth. However, the response that I found most shocking of a company of their quality, or perceived quality was "well the phone cases are contracted out and we don't directly oversee the quality control process"... So you put your name on a product that you don't properly vet. That's interesting... I also heard from someone that worked there that this wasn't the first time they've had issues with the quality of the phone cases... They offered me store credit to return my phone since it wasn't "re-sellable" I thought that was laughable, you can't even guarantee the quality of the products that in my mind should be simplest to guarantee. I'm sure, since I was assured that the leather and craftsmanship is contracted out, this isn't representative of the workmanship of the company as a whole. However, to leave me on the hook for something that you sell being sub-par is interesting to say the least... Not to mention before this phone case I had a similar authentic Italian leather case from Apple that cost $40 and held up significantly better than this has. I'm not saying I'll never shop with them again, I'm not that type of person, however right now I have a bad taste in my mouth with the company and I can find arguably comparable products for $10 and less on Amazon or Wish that last substantially longer if I wanted. This place is an example of great idea, poor execution. 1) There is a server stand with 2 people that do nothing but point to the direction of your table. They don't walk you to your table, they don't get a high chair if you need it. They literally stand there, call you when a table is open, then point you to the ground floor or second floor. Why does that take 2 people? 2) Cafeteria style dining is when you can get different foods easily and then pay at the end. Not here. You have to go to each different vendor and order, pay, then get your food. Also, you tip before receiving your food so....how much should you tip? Who cares? This place doesn't care or they would have designed a better system. Poor execution. 3) When you do get a table inside, your server only brings you drinks. You still need to go get your food from the non-cafeteria style mess of restaurants. So, the server is only getting tips on drinks and you have to pay again after already paying for your food. The server is getting drinks that I could just go get myself while waiting for my food? Why would you design it this way? I'm pretty sure 80% of our time here was waiting on food, drinks, and the check. Poor execution. Colombus OH, Chicago IL, Seattle WA, NYC NY, these are all places that are doing this well. Here's what needs to happen. 1) Don't make people stand in line at each place. Get a software system that each vendor must use and patrons can place their order at one time for every vendor. Or, order your food at each place and then pay at the end (a worse option but still better than how it is now). A patron should be able to order Nachos and a hot dog at once. Otherwise, it's not cafeteria style, it's a food court. This would cause less confusion for the vendors, and it would make everything go so much faster since you aren't processing a payment 5 different times. Also, it would likely increase sales as I would have ordered more food from different vendors but was not willing to stand in line again. Currently, it actually punishes patrons for wanting to experience all of the diverse food options. 2) If you are going to have servers, then have them serve food and drink. Otherwise, get rid of servers. I'm already waiting on the food. It's not like it's saving any time to have them just bring drinks. It's okay to not have servers. That's how most other cities do it. 3) I would assume most people are coming to Sun King to get some alcohol. Why not put it close to the door? This isn't a big deal, but it just shows that whoever designed this did not think through it. 4) Save your vendors time and have a central place for to-go containers, napkins, utensils, and condiments. This is just basic. There is currently no leverage of having 5 vendors in one spot. Even food courts do this. 5) Make it simple and enjoyable for patrons. We waited for 30 minutes to get a table to then be told we still need to wait in line and order our food. What?! What is the benefit of sitting inside? Please, please, go visit other, true cafeteria-style dining places and make changes. This could be so cool, but it's currently run like a madhouse.
